blocks.text: Jennifer Frazier, Chief Operating Officer, {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}
Dear Ms. Frazier,

Thank you for entrusting us with this search. We are glad to set down in writing the assignment we discussed, so that both sides begin from the same understanding. You have asked us to find and help you appoint a new independent director to your board. It is work we care about, and we will carry it with the discretion it deserves.
The search we have agreed

You have asked us to identify and recruit an independent director for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}, someone whose judgment will strengthen the board on the matters most in front of you. We will build a considered picture of the field, approach the strongest prospects with care, and bring you a short, well-qualified slate to interview. Throughout, we will describe candidates by the seats they hold rather than by name, and nothing about the search will travel more widely than it must. Our work does not end at the introduction; we stay with you through the interviews, the references, and the appointment itself.

Our method is unhurried and thorough. We map the relevant market, weigh each prospect against the specification we settle with you, and reference the finalists properly before any offer is made. Where a strong director is not looking to move, we still make the approach; the best board members are seldom the ones who put themselves forward. You will hear from us on a steady rhythm, not only when there is a milestone to report. A short, strong slate serves you better than a long one, and it is what we aim for.
What the search will ask of you

A search goes best when the client stays close to it. We will ask for an early conversation to agree the specification, prompt feedback as we present candidates, and a single point of contact on your side, which we understand will be you. When we reach interviews, your board's availability tends to set the pace, and we will plan around it, with Jeffrey handling the diaries so that you do not have to. None of this is heavy; a search of this length asks for a few hours of the board's attention at the right moments, no more.
The people who will do the work

You will be in steady hands. James Grant, our Senior Consultant, will lead the assignment and will be your point of contact on the assessment of candidates; board mandates are his particular strength. Jason Bell, our Research Associate, will run the market mapping and the research bench, and he has a good eye for the strong director who is not on the obvious list. Jeffrey Patterson, our Research Consultant, will manage the candidate conversations and the scheduling, and will make sure no thread goes quiet. I will stay close to the work myself, and I am always glad to take your call.
How we will keep you informed

You will not have to chase us for news. We will send a short written update on a regular cadence, and we will call the moment something needs your judgment, not wait for the next note. When we present the slate, you will have a written read on each candidate, framed by the seat held and measured against the specification we set together. Between updates, Jeffrey Patterson is your point of contact for anything that will not keep.
Our fee and the timetable

This is a retained assignment, at a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2017-001.fee}}. That figure covers the whole of the search: the research, the approaches, the assessment, and the reference work behind a finalist. We expect the work to run about four months from the day we begin, which will be {{fact:f:E-2017-001.start}}. Searches of this kind sometimes move faster and occasionally take a little longer, and we will tell you plainly if the timetable shifts.
How the fee is billed
We bill the retainer in three parts, so that our invoicing follows the progress of the work:

items: One third on our commencement of the search,
A second third when we present the qualified slate for your interviews, and
The final third on the appointment of a director.

blocks.text: Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses, such as travel to meet a candidate on your behalf, are billed at cost and itemized, and we will clear anything unusual with you before we incur it. Invoices are payable within thirty days of receipt.
The term, and how either of us may end it

The engagement runs until a director is appointed or until we close the search by agreement. Either of us may end it on reasonable written notice. Should you decide to stop the search before it is complete, you will owe us only for the work done to that point and the fees already invoiced, and nothing more. If a concern ever arises on your side, we would want to hear it early and work it through with you.
Confidentiality

Discretion is the heart of how we work. We will hold in confidence all that you share with us about the board, the company, and your reasons for the search, and we will protect the identity of every candidate with equal care. We ask the same of you in return, that the names we bring you stay within the small circle of people who need them. This protects the candidates who trust us with their interest, and it protects the search itself.
The limits of our responsibility

We will bring our full judgment and effort to the assignment, and we choose our words about a candidate with care. We cannot, however, guarantee the future performance of any director you appoint, and our liability to you is limited to the fees paid under this engagement. Where a failing is genuinely ours, we will make it good, and we would not hide behind this clause.
Governing law

This letter, and the engagement it describes, are governed by the laws of the state in which our firm is established. Anything not addressed here we will resolve as we resolve most things, by talking it through in good faith.

If this reflects our understanding, the next step is a simple one. If anything in these terms would sit better a different way, tell me before you sign; otherwise please countersign below and return one copy to me. On receipt we will schedule the kickoff and begin the market work. I am delighted that you have chosen us, and I look forward to getting started.
To: Search team, James Grant and Jeffrey Patterson. From: Jason Bell. Re: kickoff of the board director search for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}.
Objective

We have been retained to identify and recruit an independent director for the client's board. The search runs about four months. This memo records where we start and who owns what. The deliverable is a slate, not a single name. The board chooses; we find and qualify the field.
The brief is a board seat, not an executive hire. That changes the field. We are looking for judgment, sector credibility, and the standing to be heard in the room, more than day-to-day availability.

The sectors to map are the ones the board named as priorities. Within them, we look first at sitting non-executive directors and recently retired senior operators, and second at strong functional leaders ready for a first board seat. Jason Bell will draw the field from public filings, board rosters, and our own network.
Our client contact is Jennifer Frazier, Chief Operating Officer. All client communication routes through her unless she directs otherwise. The engagement began on {{fact:f:E-2017-001.start}}.

Reporting cadence is a short weekly note to the client and this internal thread kept current. Jeffrey owns the client scheduling. Jason owns the research updates. James owns anything that touches the specification or assessment.
What a good outcome looks like

A good outcome is a short slate of three or four genuine prospects the board is glad to interview. Each name has to be a real candidate, not a name to fill the list. We aim for a small, strong slate, not a long one. If the specification holds through the first approaches without rework, the calibration was right. If prospects push back on the profile, we adjust the specification at once and re-map.
Lines of work

items: Market map and long list. Owner: Jason Bell. Build the field of prospective directors from current and recent board and senior operating roles.
Specification. Owner: James Grant, with the client. Agree the profile, the priorities, and any firm requirements before outreach opens.
Candidate approaches and care. Owner: Jeffrey Patterson. Manage first contact, interest, and scheduling; keep every thread current.
Assessment and references. Owner: James Grant. Test the advancing candidates against the specification and lead the reference work.
Client updates. Owner: Jeffrey Patterson. Send a short weekly note to the client and keep this internal thread current.

blocks.text: Timeline

We are early. The first weeks are market work and specification. The middle weeks are approaches and first conversations. The back weeks are assessment, references, and interviews. We hold to that sequence unless the client's needs move it. We are in the first block now. No approaches go out until the specification is confirmed.
Discipline

One standing rule. We describe candidates by their current seat, never by name, in anything that circulates. The strongest prospects are often people who are not looking to move, so first approaches are discreet and go out only once the specification is set.
Immediate steps

First actions are set. Jason Bell opens the market map now. James Grant drafts the specification for the client call. Jeffrey Patterson holds two interview windows in reserve so we are not chasing diaries later. Early feedback matters more than usual here, so we calibrate the specification hard in the first two weeks and adjust the map fast if the client's read differs from ours. By the internal review, the long list should sit at a workable size, roughly two to three dozen names, before any narrowing begins.

We regroup at the end of the first fortnight to review the long list. Flag anything that needs the client before then. Keep the client thread and this one current; a search stalls when a note sits unanswered.
Good morning Jennifer,

A short update on the board search for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}. The market map is built, and we have begun reading the strongest prospects against the specification we agreed. We approach a first group of prospective directors this week. Two prospects I did not expect have already surfaced, which is the part of this work I enjoy most. The specification is holding well against the market, which is a good sign this early, and as throughout we describe candidates by their current seat, not by name. None of the strongest names has ruled itself out.

The team on this is steady. I am your day-to-day contact on the research, Jason Bell, with James Grant leading the assessment and Jeffrey Patterson keeping the candidate conversations and scheduling in hand. No thread is going quiet, and you will have a fuller written status from us shortly. If a name ever needs your steer, James will bring it to you himself.

One ask, so that we do not lose time later. When the slate is ready, your board's interview availability will set our pace. Could you hold two provisional windows over the coming weeks? I will have Jeffrey firm them up as candidates confirm, and he will work through you alone, Jennifer Frazier, so that nothing about the search travels wider than it should. Even rough placeholders help; we can confirm the times later as candidates lock in.
Sincerely,
Working Session, Board Director Search for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}

The purpose of this session was to review progress on the board director search since kickoff, to calibrate the specification against what the early market work has surfaced, and to agree the sequence of steps that will carry us toward a qualified slate; these minutes record, in order, who attended, what was discussed, and what each of us undertook to do.
Present
Progress since kickoff

Jason Bell presented the state of the market map, which now covers the relevant field of prospective directors drawn from current and recent board and senior operating roles across the sectors we agreed to prioritize, and he noted that the long list has reached a workable size without yet having been narrowed, so that no prospect has been set aside prematurely. He added that two prospects had surfaced whom none of us had expected, which he took as a sign that the map is reaching beyond the obvious names.

Jennifer Frazier gave the client's read on the profile, emphasizing that the board values sector credibility and the standing to be heard in the room over a simple count of prior directorships, and she asked that we give weight to candidates whose experience speaks to the board's current priorities, a point that we agreed to fold directly into the specification. She also confirmed that the board would prefer a genuinely independent voice to a familiar one, which narrows the field in a useful way.

On the specification itself, we recorded the profile as it now stands: an independent director with credibility in the relevant sector, the standing to be heard in the room, freedom from conflict with the company, and the time to serve as a working member of the board rather than a name on the letterhead.

On the question of pace, we set out the ordinary rhythm of a search of this kind, in which the long list is refined into a shorter roster of genuine prospects, those prospects are approached and assessed in sequence, and only a small, well-qualified group is brought forward for interview; we are presently at the refining stage, well short of finalists, and we were candid that the calibration now underway is what most determines the quality of the slate later on.

We reviewed, in turn, the discipline that governs how this search is conducted: every candidate is described by the seat presently held rather than by name in any material that circulates, and the first approaches, which Jeffrey Patterson is managing, will be made discreetly to those who are not themselves seeking a move, since the strongest board members are seldom those who put themselves forward.

We closed the discussion by fixing the shape of the next review, at which Jason Bell will bring the refined long list, James Grant will bring the revised specification for confirmation, and Jennifer Frazier will bring the board's read on interview timing, so that the session can move us cleanly from research into approaches without a further round of calibration.
Actions agreed

rows: Revise the position specification to reflect the client's weighting and circulate it for confirmation
Refine the long list against the sharpened specification and prepare a first cut for internal review
Open discreet approaches to the priority prospects and hold provisional interview windows
Confirm the revised specification and the board's interview availability

blocks.text: Our single next step is the confirmation of the revised specification; once Jennifer Frazier returns it, we will open the priority approaches and set the date on which we present the first cut of the slate for review.
Board Director Search for {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}: Status at the Midpoint
Summary

The search is on track and roughly at its midpoint. The market work is complete. The long list has been refined to a working roster of genuine prospects, and first approaches are underway. Nothing at this stage gives cause for concern, and we expect to hold the timetable we set. Since our last note, the map has closed and outreach has begun. The move from research to candidate contact is the main change to report.
Progress this period

items: Position specification agreed with you and stable since.
Market map complete across the priority sectors.
Long list refined to a working roster of genuine prospects.
First discreet approaches opened; early interest encouraging.

blocks.text: James Grant led the specification and the assessment framework. Jason Bell built the market map and the long list. Jeffrey Patterson is managing the approaches and the candidate conversations, and is keeping every thread current. Every prospect we approach is logged, with their current seat and their read on a possible move, so the roster stays current from one week to the next.

Response to the first approaches has been better than typical for a board mandate. Several of the strongest prospects have agreed to an exploratory conversation, and none of the names we most wanted has declined. That is a good position at the halfway mark. We will keep the pressure on outreach so the momentum holds into the second half.

The field breaks into three groups. There are sitting non-executive directors at comparable companies, recently retired senior operators with the standing for a board seat, and a smaller set of strong first-time directors with deep functional experience. We are weighting the first two, in line with the specification. The third group is thinner but worth carrying, since a first-time director with the right functional depth can be the freshest voice in the room. As always, we describe each candidate by the seat now held rather than by name.

The specification is doing its job. It asks for judgment, credibility in the relevant sector, and the standing to be heard in a boardroom, ahead of a long directorship record. It sets no hard bar on prior board count. It does ask that a candidate be free of conflict with the company and able to give the time a working director needs. We have held it as written, and it is keeping the roster focused.
The weeks ahead

The next phase turns the roster into a slate. We will complete the priority approaches, hold first conversations, and assess those who advance against the specification. We expect to present a short, qualified slate for your interviews in the back half of the engagement.

Assessment is structured, not impressionistic. Each advancing candidate is measured against the same specification, on the record, so that the comparison you see is a fair one. You will have our written read on every name we put forward, framed by the seat held.

Reference work follows selection, it does not precede it. We check each finalist properly, and discreetly, before any offer is discussed, since none of these candidates has spoken to a current employer.
So that we do not lose time when the slate is ready, it will help to hold provisional interview windows now. Jeffrey Patterson will coordinate the dates as candidates confirm.
Risks and watch items

Two items warrant attention, neither serious. First, board searches turn on the availability of people who are not looking to move, so a strong prospect may step aside on timing even when the fit is right. We manage this by carrying enough depth in the roster that no single withdrawal sets us back. We are carrying more names in the priority tier than the slate will need, for exactly this reason.

Second, interview scheduling across a full board is the most common cause of delay late in a search. Reserving windows now is the surest guard against it. We see no risk to confidentiality; the search is holding tightly.
What will help from you

Two things from your side will keep the closing weeks clean. First, hold the provisional interview windows we have asked for; late scheduling is the usual cause of slippage. Second, when you are ready, confirm the compensation and time expectations for the seat, so that we can be straight with candidates from the first serious conversation.
Budget

The engagement is a retained assignment at a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2017-001.fee}}, which covers the search in full, from the research through the reference work behind a finalist. We are within that fee. We expect no charges beyond it, save the itemized expenses set out in our agreement.
We will send the next written status at the three-quarter mark, or sooner if the slate firms up before then. Between reports, Jeffrey Patterson is your point of contact for anything time-sensitive.
Our single priority before the next report is to complete the priority approaches and firm up the interview windows. We will send the qualified slate as soon as the first conversations are done.
